overview: Finland is a country in northern Europe, between Sweden and Russia. Its capital and largest city is Helsinki. Finland was part of Sweden for centuries and then part of the Russian Empire, before becoming independent in 1917. Finnish and Swedish are both official languages. Finland joined the European Union in 1995 and NATO in 2023.

geography.text: Finland is often called the land of a thousand lakes, but it actually has many tens of thousands. Forests cover around three-quarters of the country. The land is mostly low and gently rolling, shaped by ice sheets during the last Ice Age. The north lies within the Arctic Circle, in Lapland, where the sun does not set for weeks in midsummer.

history.text: For about 600 years Finland was part of the Kingdom of Sweden. In 1809 it became a grand duchy of the Russian Empire, and it declared independence in 1917, during the Russian Revolution. Finland fought the Soviet Union in the Second World War and kept its independence, and later built one of the world's most successful welfare states.

events.title: Russian rule
events.text: Sweden loses Finland to Russia, which makes it a grand duchy.

events.title: Votes for women
events.text: Finland becomes the first country in Europe to give women the vote and the right to stand for parliament.

events.title: Winter War
events.text: Finland fights off a Soviet invasion, though it loses some territory.

events.title: Joins NATO
events.text: Finland becomes a member of NATO.
